title: Checkpoint relation preserves halting
statement: Let $c$ be an effective machine-coding scheme, let $\alpha$ and $x$ be finite Boolean words, let $s$ be a configuration of the machine decoded from $\alpha$ on input $x$, and let $d$ be a configuration of the associated universal machine on $\langle\alpha,x\rangle$. If $s$ and $d$ satisfy the checkpoint relation, then $s$ is halted if and only if $d$ is halted.
hypotheses_covered: $s$ is a configuration of the decoded machine on input $x$
$d$ is a configuration of the associated universal machine on $\langle\alpha,x\rangle$
replaced:
Let $c$ be an effective machine-coding scheme, let $\alpha$ and $x$ be finite bit
strings, and let $s$ be a configuration of the machine decoded from $\alpha$ on input
$x$. Let $t$ be a configuration of the universal machine associated with $c$ on the
encoding of $\alpha$ and $x$. If the checkpoint relation holds between $s$ and $t$, then
$s$ is halted if and only if $t$ is halted.
